# fluid error codes

Every failure prints a stable `ERR_<EVENT>` code next to its message. Find the
code here and do what the first suggestion says, then re-run the command. A code
missing from this table has no curated advice: read the message it printed.
Docs pages are relative to https://agenticstiger.github.io/forge_docs/

| Code | What to do | Docs page |
|---|---|---|
| `ERR_PROVIDER_NOT_SPECIFIED` | Pass a provider: --provider aws\|databricks\|gcp\|local\|snowflake. Or set the FLUID_PROVIDER environment variable. Run 'fluid providers' to list the available providers. | cli/providers.html |
| `ERR_PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND` | Run 'fluid providers' to see the available providers. Check the provider name spelling. Install the provider extra, e.g. pip install 'data-product-forge[gcp]'. | cli/providers.html |
| `ERR_PROVIDER_UNKNOWN` | Run 'fluid providers' to see the available providers. Valid built-ins: aws, databricks, gcp, local, snowflake. | cli/providers.html |
| `ERR_PROVIDER_LOAD_FAILED` | The provider is declared but importing it failed (see the WARNING above). Reinstall the distribution named in the error, or its extra. Run 'fluid providers --debug' for the discovery errors. | cli/providers.html |
| `ERR_PROVIDER_RETIRED` | Run 'fluid providers' to see the available providers. CHANGELOG.md lists it under Removed, with its replacement. | cli/providers.html |
| `ERR_APPLY_PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED` | If a job outside forge-cli (a Flink job, say) writes that expose or is that build, declare the build with engine: flink (or properties.language: flink_sql) and outputs naming what it writes: forge-cli then leaves both to the job. --provider <name> (or FLUID_PROVIDER) applies the whole contract with the provider you name; the local provider writes a binding it does not serve as a placeholder file. | cli/providers.html |
| `ERR_APPLY_PLAN_RUNS_OUTSIDE_FORGE` | In the default mode, apply the contract file instead (fluid apply contract.fluid.yaml): the local planner plans it, and leaves what a job outside forge-cli writes to that job. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_PROVIDER_BLOCKED_BY_POLICY` | This provider is named in FLUID_PLUGINS_BLOCKLIST, or an FLUID_PLUGINS_ALLOWLIST is set and does not name it. Run 'fluid plugins --role provider' to see the effective policy. Unset or amend the env var to re-enable it. | cli/providers.html |
| `ERR_RESERVED_PROVIDER_NAME` | Choose a provider name that is not a reserved built-in. | cli/providers.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_REQUIRED` | Pass the contract path: fluid <command> path/to/contract.fluid.yaml. Or run from a directory that contains a single contract.fluid.yaml. Scaffold one with 'fluid init' or 'fluid forge'. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_NOT_FOUND` | Check that the contract file path is correct. Ensure the file has a .yaml, .yml, or .json extension. Scaffold one with 'fluid init' or 'fluid forge'. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_FILE_NOT_FOUND` | Check that the contract file path is correct. Run 'ls *.fluid.yaml' to see contracts in the current directory. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_LOAD_FAILED` | Verify the YAML/JSON syntax is valid. Check file permissions and that the encoding is UTF-8. Run 'fluid validate <contract>' for a detailed report. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_INVALID_SCHEMA_VERSION` | Use a supported version (current line: 0.7.x) in fluidVersion or --schema-version. Run 'fluid validate --list-versions' to see the supported versions. | advanced/typed-cli-errors.html#validation-schema |
| `ERR_SCHEMA_VERSION_REQUIRED` | Name the version: fluid validate --fragment KIND <file> --schema-version <version>. Run 'fluid validate --list-versions' to see the supported versions. | advanced/typed-cli-errors.html#validation-schema |
| `ERR_FRAGMENT_FILE_REQUIRED` | Give the kind, then the file: fluid validate --fragment expose <file>. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_FRAGMENT_BUNDLE_UNSUPPORTED` | Validate the bundle without --fragment: fluid validate <bundle>.tgz. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_FRAGMENT_KIND_UNKNOWN` | Use one of the kinds the error lists, for example: fluid validate --fragment expose <file>. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_FRAGMENT_ENV_UNSUPPORTED` | Validate the whole contract with the overlay: fluid validate contract.fluid.yaml --env <env>. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_FRAGMENT_HAS_POINTERS` | Validate the contract that uses the fragment: fluid validate contract.fluid.yaml. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEMA_NOT_AVAILABLE` | Run 'fluid validate --list-versions' to see the versions this CLI has. | advanced/typed-cli-errors.html#validation-schema |
| `ERR_CONTRACT_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED` | Migrate the contract to the current 0.7.x schema. Pre-0.7 contracts (0.4.0 / 0.5.x) are no longer supported. | advanced/typed-cli-errors.html#validation-schema |
| `ERR_INVALID_MIN_VERSION` | Give --min-version a version constraint, for example --min-version '>=0.7.0'. | advanced/typed-cli-errors.html#validation-schema |
| `ERR_INVALID_MAX_VERSION` | Give --max-version a version constraint, for example --max-version '<0.8.0'. | advanced/typed-cli-errors.html#validation-schema |
| `ERR_VALIDATION_FAILED` | Run 'fluid validate <contract> --verbose' for the full error list. Check required fields and the schema reference for your fluidVersion. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_VALIDATION_ERROR` | Run 'fluid validate <contract> --verbose' for details. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_BUNDLE_NOT_FOUND` | Run 'fluid bundle <contract> --format tgz' to produce a bundle first. Check the bundle path you passed. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_BUNDLE_MANIFEST_INVALID` | Re-create the bundle with 'fluid bundle' — the manifest is malformed. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_BUNDLE_MISSING_CONTRACT` | Re-create the bundle with 'fluid bundle' — it has no contract entry. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_PLANNER_FAILED` | Run 'fluid validate <contract>' first to rule out a contract problem. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_APPLY_BUILD_IDENTIFIER_INVALID` | Rename the id to fit, for example orders_v1 instead of 1orders, and apply again. A renamed id starts over: its builds get new cursors and watermarks under .fluid/runs/, and a renamed contract.id gets a new OpenTofu workdir under .fluid/iac/<provider>/. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_APPLY_BUILD_ID_NOT_FOUND` | Pass one of the available build ids as --build-id: ids match exactly, case included. Run 'fluid apply <contract> --mode amend-and-build' without --build-id to run every build. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_OUTPUT_WRITE_FAILED` | Check that the --out path is writable and the parent directory exists. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_OPENTOFU_ENGINE_INSTALL_FAILED` | Install OpenTofu >= 1.6.0 and ensure 'tofu' is on PATH. See https://opentofu.org/docs/intro/install/. | getting-started/ |
| `ERR_OPENTOFU_INIT_FAILED` | Check provider credentials and network access, then retry. | advanced/typed-cli-errors.html#connectivity-secrets |
| `ERR_OPENTOFU_PLAN_FAILED` | Run 'fluid plan <contract>' and inspect the emitted plan for the failing action. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_OPENTOFU_APPLY_FAILED` | OpenTofu records state as it goes, so resources created before the failure are normally tracked. Fix the cause named above, then re-run 'fluid apply' to continue. Re-run with --debug to see the raw tofu output. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_OPENTOFU_ADOPTION_FAILED` | Check the provider credentials and network access, then re-run 'fluid apply'. The apply stopped before planning: it could not tell whether the object exists, and creating over it would replace it. | advanced/typed-cli-errors.html#connectivity-secrets |
| `ERR_OPENTOFU_REGION_MOVED` | If the resources should stay where they are, set the binding's location.region to the region the error names. If they should move, empty and remove them there first (tofu destroy in the state directory the error names, with AWS_REGION set to the old region), then apply again. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_COPILOT_MISSING_LLM_API_KEY` | Run 'fluid ai setup' to configure a provider interactively. Or set a provider key: OPENAI_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / GEMINI_API_KEY. For local models: --llm-provider ollama (no key required). For keyless authoring: run forge from your IDE (mcp-sampling) or --llm-provider claude-code. | cli/secrets.html |
| `ERR_COPILOT_NO_LLM_PROVIDER` | Pass --llm-provider, for example anthropic, openai, gemini or ollama. Or set FLUID_LLM_PROVIDER, or the API key of exactly one provider. Or run 'fluid ai setup' to choose and save a provider. Run 'fluid doctor' to see what forge would select. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_COPILOT_LITELLM_UNAVAILABLE` | Run 'fluid doctor' to see which optional packages are installed. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_MCP_SDK_UNAVAILABLE` | Run 'fluid doctor' to see which optional packages are installed. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CLAUDE_SETTINGS_NOT_VALID_JSON` | Fix the JSON syntax in the named .claude/settings.json (or settings.local.json). Re-run: fluid scaffold-ide --target claude-code. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CLAUDE_SETTINGS_UNEXPECTED_SHAPE` | The named settings file must be a JSON object; if it has 'hooks', that must be an object, and 'hooks.PostToolUse' a list of objects. Fix the file, then re-run: fluid scaffold-ide --target claude-code. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_CLAUDE_SETTINGS_LINKS_OUTSIDE_PROJECT` | The named Claude Code settings file is a symlink to a file outside this project; scaffold-ide would copy that file's content into the project. Replace the link with a regular file or delete it, then re-run: fluid scaffold-ide --target claude-code. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCAFFOLD_IDE_FILE_NOT_UTF8` | Re-save the named CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md as UTF-8. Then re-run: fluid scaffold-ide --target <target>. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCAFFOLD_IDE_BLOCK_MARKERS_MALFORMED` | The named CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md must hold either no scaffold-ide markers or exactly one '<!-- BEGIN forge-cli scaffold-ide block -->' followed by one matching END marker. Delete the stray or duplicate marker lines (the file was left untouched), then re-run: fluid scaffold-ide --target <target>. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_REFUSING_TO_OVERWRITE_EXISTING_FILE_PASS_FORCE_TO_OVERRIDE` | Re-run with --force to replace the file: fluid scaffold-ide --target <target> --force. --force keeps the text of CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md outside the scaffold-ide block. Upgrading? --force also removes the steering files an earlier scaffold-ide wrote. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_OPTIONAL_DEPENDENCY_MISSING` | Run 'fluid doctor' to see which optional packages are installed. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_COPILOT_MISSING_LLM_MODEL` | Set FLUID_LLM_MODEL or pass --llm-model. Run 'fluid ai setup' to pick a default model. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_COPILOT_LLM_MODEL_PREFLIGHT_FAILED` | Check the provider API key and network connectivity. For Ollama, start the local server and pull the requested model. Pass --llm-model with a known-available model. | advanced/typed-cli-errors.html#connectivity-secrets |
| `ERR_MODEL_NOT_FOUND` | Run 'fluid ai setup' to pick a model the provider actually serves. List the provider's models, then pass --llm-model <name>. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_MISSING_CONTRACT` | Pass the contract path: fluid <command> path/to/contract.fluid.yaml. Or run from a directory that contains a single contract.fluid.yaml. Scaffold one with 'fluid init' or 'fluid forge'. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_LOADER_IMPORT_FAILED` | Check that the loader module path is importable (on PYTHONPATH). Verify the module has no syntax/import errors: python -c 'import <module>'. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_LOADER_MISSING_FUNCTIONS` | The loader module must define the required entry-point functions — check its API. Define the expected functions (e.g. load/run) — see the custom-loader docs. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_GENERATE_IAC_FAILED` | Run 'fluid validate <contract>' first to rule out a contract problem. Re-run with --provider explicitly set if auto-detect picked the wrong cloud. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_GENERATE_IAC_PROVIDER_MISMATCH` | Drop --provider and let the cloud auto-detect from the contract's binding. Or change the contract's exposes[].binding.platform to the cloud you meant to target — that is how a data product is retargeted, not --provider. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_GENERATE_IAC_EMPTY_MODULE` | Check the contract's exposes[].binding carries the location fields the target cloud's emitter needs (bucket/dataset/database). Run 'fluid validate <contract>' — the Iceberg and Confluent binding gates name the specific field a skipped resource was missing. Pass --allow-empty only if a resource-free module is genuinely intended. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_GENERATE_IAC_AWS_ACCOUNT_REQUIRED` | Set AWS_ACCOUNT_ID to the account the module will be applied in, then re-run 'fluid generate iac' (it never looks the account up in AWS). 'fluid apply' resolves the account itself and needs no AWS_ACCOUNT_ID. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_GENERATE_CI_FAILED` | Check the --system value is a supported CI provider and the contract validates. Run 'fluid validate <contract>', then re-run with a supported --system (github_actions\|gitlab\|jenkins\|azure_devops\|...). | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_NO_BUILDS` | No build runners matched — check the contract's build/transform config. Run 'fluid apply <contract> --mode amend-and-build' only when builds are defined. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_VERIFY_FAILED` | Run 'fluid verify <contract> --verbose' to see which reconciliation check failed. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_POLICY_COMPILE_FAILED` | Check the agent-policy block in the contract; run 'fluid policy check <contract>'. | concepts/sovereignty.html |
| `ERR_POLICY_COMPILER_CRASHED` | Run 'fluid validate <contract>': policy compile reads accessPolicy and exposes without validating them against the contract schema. If the contract validates, re-run with 'fluid --log-level DEBUG policy compile <contract>' to see the compiler's traceback. | cli/policy-compile.html#errors |
| `ERR_POLICY_APPLY_FAILED` | Run 'fluid policy check <contract>' to surface the offending rule before apply. | concepts/sovereignty.html |
| `ERR_SOVEREIGNTY_VIOLATION` | Move the offending binding into an allowed region, or widen 'sovereignty.allowedRegions' in the contract. Run 'fluid validate <contract>' to see the same findings with full detail. Set 'sovereignty.enforcementMode: advisory' to report without blocking. | concepts/sovereignty.html |
| `ERR_PRODUCT_NEW_FAILED` | Check the target directory is writable and the productType is valid (SDP/ADP/CDP). Pick an empty/new target dir and pass --data-product-type SDP\|ADP\|CDP explicitly. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_PRODUCT_ADD_FAILED` | Run 'fluid validate' on the contract first; --type must be source\|exposure\|dq. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_PRODUCT_ADD_EXPOSE_NOT_FOUND` | The --expose target does not exist in the contract — list exposes with 'fluid status'. Add the expose first, or target an existing exposeId. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_BUNDLE_SOURCE_MISSING` | Re-create the bundle with 'fluid bundle' — a referenced source file is absent. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_BUNDLE_LOAD_FAILED` | The bundle is corrupt or truncated — re-create it with 'fluid bundle <contract>'. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_MARKET_DISCOVERY_FAILED` | Check network access to the marketplace endpoint (FLUID_MARKET_URL). Bundled blueprints work offline: 'fluid market --blueprints'. | advanced/typed-cli-errors.html#connectivity-secrets |
| `ERR_MISSING_BLUEPRINT_PARAMETER` | The blueprint requires a parameter — pass it with --param key=value. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SIGNING_BUNDLE_MISSING` | Produce the bundle first ('fluid bundle <contract> --format tgz'), then sign it. | cli/verify-signature.html |
| `ERR_SIGNING_BUNDLE_NOT_FILE` | The signing target must be a bundle file, not a directory. Produce one with 'fluid bundle <contract> --format tgz', then sign that .tgz. | cli/verify-signature.html |
| `ERR_SIGNING_KEY_REF_EMPTY` | Provide a signing key reference (e.g. a cosign key or KMS key URI). See the signing setup in the supply-chain docs. | cli/verify-signature.html |
| `ERR_VALIDATE_ARTIFACTS_INPUT_MISSING` | Pass the generated-artifacts path produced by 'fluid generate artifacts'. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_DAGS_DIR_MISSING` | Pass --dags-dir pointing at your Airflow DAGs directory. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_DAGS_DIR_NOT_DIRECTORY` | The --dags-dir value must be an existing directory. Create it (mkdir -p) or point --dags-dir at your Airflow dags/ folder. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_SCHEDULE_SYNC_UNHANDLED_SCHEME` | Use a supported destination scheme (file / scp / git+ssh) for --to. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_ROLLBACK_PRODUCT_ID_EMPTY` | Pass the product id to roll back: fluid rollback <product-id>. | advanced/production-troubleshooting.html |
| `ERR_ICEBERG_CATALOG_MOVE_BLOCKED` | Run the printed `tofu state rm` commands: they release the resources from this contract's OpenTofu state and touch nothing in the cloud. Then re-run fluid apply. The released Glue database/table or Snowflake EXTERNAL VOLUME stays in place; delete it by hand only if nothing else uses it. | cli/apply.html#iceberg-catalog-move-guard |
